## Demo receipt photos and merchant name — October 18, 2026 (Saahil)
Demo photo scans now go to Gemini. The new server method `readReceiptPhoto(photo, {merchant, amount})` runs before the sign-in check. It validates the photo the same way `scanReceipt` does, and returns `{read}` or 503 `scan_off` / 502 `scan_failed` / 400 `bad_photo` / 400 `bad_charge`. `index.ts` limits it to 6 reads per minute per IP, returning 429 `rate_limited`. In demo mode, `api.ts` calls it with the publishable key and passes the read to the local `scanReceipt` / `parseReceipt`. Until the `rpc` function is redeployed, the live server answers "Unknown method." for demo photos. The Apple Pay screen now has an editable Merchant field (default Blue Bottle, max 60 characters) next to the amount; the purchase and the Payment confirmed page use that name. Server, mobile, typecheck and lint checks pass.

## Receipt photos — October 17, 2026 (Saahil)
With shared accounts, the cardholder can take or choose a photo of the receipt on the Split tab. The app shrinks it to a 1568px JPEG and sends it with `scanReceipt`. The server first checks the caller could scan that charge, then asks a Gemini vision model (`gemini-3.5-flash-lite` by default, set by `GEMINI_MODEL`; Claude is the fallback when only `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set) once for items, tax and tip, outside the write retry loop. The read only becomes the claim board if it adds up exactly to the charge; otherwise Gemini's lines stay as a draft nobody can claim, and the board opens only after a save that matches. A client can't submit its own read. "Use sample receipt" keeps the sample scanner. The local demo sends a real photo to `readReceiptPhoto`, which needs no sign-in, reads nothing from the database and saves nothing: the browser sends the photo plus the charge's merchant and amount, and runs `fromScan` on Gemini's read against its own copy of the charge. The Edge Function allows 6 of these reads per minute per IP. Capture and upload run inside Connor's first-send controller and wait for the app to return to the foreground, so opening the camera, cancelling, or a failed upload doesn't send the default split.
Implementation: `supabase/functions/rpc/receipt.ts` (model call, photo checks), `core.ts` (photo preflight; 503 `scan_off` when neither key is set, 502 `scan_failed`, 400 for bad photos), `domain.ts` `scanReceipt(..., read?)`, `fakeOcr.ts` `fromScan`, `mobile/src/lib/photo.ts`, Split's scan prompt; adds `expo-image-picker` and `expo-image-manipulator`, and the first-send test now runs in `npm test`. TypeScript, lint, mobile, network and server tests pass. The live Gemini read is in the deployed-server note above. A check on two physical phones is still outstanding.

## Optional one-purchase lock — October 17, 2026 (Saahil)
The one-open-charge rule (schema 2.v) is now a group setting, on by default. With it off, several charges can be open at once: every open charge is held from the group fund, and a member who hasn't added their share this period has their share of every open charge held from their own balance, so the overspending concern behind the rule still holds. Withdrawals stay locked while any split is pending. Home lists every open charge, notifications and Home rows open the matching charge, and the Split tab shows a charge picker once your own draft is sent.
Implementation: `domain.ts` (data version 6, `Group.singleOpenCharge`, `openCharges`, `reservedFunds`, `setSingleOpenCharge`), seed, fake API, Home/Split/Profile; tests cover the lock, held funds and the restricted-member limit. TypeScript, lint and tests pass; clicked through in headless Chrome. `competitors.txt` 2.iv (Henry's) still says "one open charge at a time", which remains true by default.

## Spending rule and first proposal — October 17, 2026 (Saahil; supersedes parts of the next section)
Spending: balances have no minimum. A member who brought their balance up to their share at the start of the period (leftover balance counts) can spend whatever is in the group fund; a member who skipped their top-up can only spend up to their own balance until they add it. This replaces the $0 restriction. A confirmed split that takes someone below $0 charges their personal card back to $0; suspension if that fails is unchanged.
First proposal: after a purchase the charge is the cardholder's draft. They pick who was part of it and how much (or scan the receipt) and send it; only people with a share are notified. Leaving the split screen, backgrounding the app or switching demo user sends the group's default split; the fake backend also sends it after 10 minutes. Notifications show on Home as a stand-in for push.
Implementation: `domain.ts` (data version 5), seed, fake API, Split/Home/Card/Profile screens; tests cover both rules. TypeScript, lint and tests pass, and the new flows were clicked through in headless Chrome. `backend.txt` updated to match (authorization rule, saved-card debt recovery, send-default endpoint, draft job, notifications table).

## Schema update — October 17, 2026 (Connor and Saahil; supersedes parts of the next section)
`schema.txt` now defines a budget per period (e.g. $300 every 2 weeks) instead of a one-time buying power; invites by user ID/email/phone that members accept (deposit) or decline; period-start refills (automatic or manual) up to each member's share; restriction at a $0 balance until funds are added or the next period starts; automatic bank charge for negative balances after a split, with suspension (group carries the debt) if it fails; withdrawals only when no split is pending; pending splits shown under the fund amount; and an itemized claim board where each person claims and locks items, others suggest edits, and the split confirms once all items are claimed with no pending edits.
Implementation: `domain.ts` (data version 3), seed, fake API and all screens updated; new tests cover invites, periods, restriction, debt recovery/suspension, withdraw lock and the claim board. TypeScript, lint, tests and web export pass; not yet clicked through in a browser. Generative AI ideas that still fit the schema, and ones that don't, were added as section 6 of `schema.txt`.

## Product model change — October 17, 2026 (supersedes the flow below)
Connor's `schema.txt` replaces the original "approve first, then a one-time card" flow. The product is now a standing group fund: members make equal initial deposits that set the group's buying power; each member has their own virtual card on the fund; purchases are charged first and split afterwards through iterative proposals that every member with a share must accept; only one charge may be open at a time; balances are decreased on settlement and refilled by manual or automatic top-ups; members below their share are restricted to their own balance; buying power changes need unanimous acceptance; unagreed splits after 7 days and chargebacks freeze the group and escalate to a (hypothetical) dispute center; receipts can be scanned and items claimed, with tax/tip proportional to items; Activity and Profile track group and personal spend.

Implementation (October 17): the whole model is built in the Expo app against a fake backend (`mobile/src/lib/api.ts`) that enforces the rules in `mobile/src/lib/domain.ts` and persists to device storage. Split math (`mobile/src/lib/split.ts`) now supports any group size. A demo user switcher stands in for authentication. The previous single-bill engine, local recovery module and their tests were removed and replaced with split and domain tests. TypeScript, lint and tests pass; main flows were clicked through in the web preview. Next phase: real backend and APIs, then issuing/wallet partners. Earlier sections below are historical context; where they describe pre-approval before payment or a per-bill card, they no longer apply.

## Product
A social group-checkout app: friends link funding accounts, agree to flexible shares and pay a merchant with one app-issued virtual card. The merchant receives one payment; each participant sees their own obligation. Initial audience hypothesis: US college students dining in groups. Geography and hackathon deadline are unconfirmed.

## Current deliverable
Current native recovery behavior (October 16): drafts and up to 100 simulated receipts persist locally. Reopening revokes all approvals and discards card/wallet state; history is not synchronized or authenticated. The earlier in-memory description below is historical.
A private responsive browser demo with three sample participants, editable subtotal/tax/tip, equal/percentage/custom-amount splits, exact-cent allocation, per-person simulated approval, approval reset when the bill changes, simulated card readiness, decline/retry, and shared receipt. No real accounts, card issuance, money movement, authentication or cross-device synchronization. Demo state resets on refresh. Approvals are controls on one screen, not proof of participant consent. Source and this plan are stored in the Site repository; project folder contains the Site.

## Product decisions
Use an explicit simulation for judging the experience before obtaining issuer access. Treat the card as an app-issued payment credential; do not claim it is credit until the funding product is chosen. Prefer secured contributions before merchant authorization as the starting architecture hypothesis. This does not mean linked account balances or authorizations guarantee settled funds. Resolve liquidity, returns and risk with a qualified issuing partner before live payments.

The app must show total and shares before approval. Any material change invalidates approvals. Fees must be disclosed before consent. Handle tax, shared items and tip explicitly. A decline must not silently switch liability to the organizer. No fake Apple Pay button or claim that a browser demo can tap to pay.

## Initial market research — checked October 15, 2026
| Product | Verified overlap | Implication |
|---|---|---|
| Cino | Group cards, connected funding cards and adjustable split ratios; bills split at payment | Direct competitor. Do not claim this payment model is unique. |
| Venmo Groups | Shared-expense records, customized splits and payments due between members | Familiar social pattern; distinguish checkout experience from reimbursement. |
| Splitwise | Group expense tracking and flexible splitting | Flexible arithmetic alone is insufficient differentiation. |
| tricount | Shared-expense tracking, custom splits and bunq card expense tracking | Card-adjacent competitors matter as well as ledger apps. |

Sources: https://www.getcino.com/ ; https://www.balderton.com/news/cino-raises-e3-5m-to-revolutionise-shared-payments-with-the-first-virtual-card-that-splits-and-pays-group-bills-instantly/ ; https://help.venmo.com/cs/articles/managing-expenses-for-venmo-groups-vhel173 ; https://help.venmo.com/cs/articles/splitting-sharing-purchases-vhel189 ; https://www.splitwise.com/ ; https://www.tricount.com/features . Vendor descriptions establish advertised capabilities, not independent performance. Geographic availability, pricing and user adoption need additional verification.

Working differentiation hypothesis: clear item-level allocation plus explicit approval of tax/tip and predictable failure handling for ad-hoc restaurant groups. Validate this against Cino QuickSplit and split-by-amount before making competitive claims. No market-size or demand estimates have been invented.

## Payments feasibility
Stripe documents virtual cards and Issuing authorizations, test purchases and a separate approval path for live access. Consumer issuing documentation exists, but suitability and eligibility for this exact program are not established. Issuing does not by itself implement atomic multi-person funding. A viable system needs the issuer/processor, funding rails, a ledger and reconciler, identity/consent, fraud controls and operational support.
Sources: https://docs.stripe.com/api/issuing/cards/create ; https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/testing ; https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/onboarding-overview ; https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/consumer-compliance .

## Target architecture
Client -> authenticated API -> group/session service -> versioned split proposal -> participant approvals -> funding orchestration -> issuer authorization policy -> capture/reconciliation -> receipts/refunds.
Entities: User, FundingInstrumentToken, Group, Membership, Bill, LineItem, SplitVersion, Share, Approval, FundingAttempt, CardSession, Authorization, Capture, LedgerEntry, Refund, AuditEvent.
Money: integer minor units and explicit currency; largest-remainder allocation with stable participant ordering. Each write uses idempotency keys. Approvals reference immutable split version and amount. Webhooks authenticate signatures, deduplicate events and support out-of-order delivery. Ledger balances cannot be inferred solely from browser state.
States: draft -> awaiting approvals -> securing funding -> ready -> authorized -> captured; separate failed/cancelled/expired paths. Merchant authorization and final capture can differ, especially restaurant tips. Additional amounts require prior disclosed limits or renewed consent. Refunds follow original allocation and cannot exceed captured amounts. Production needs compensating actions for partial funding failures and reconciliation, not assumed distributed atomicity.

## Acceptance gates
Shares sum exactly to total. Invalid input blocks payment. Changes revoke approvals. Only all valid approvals unlock payment. Failed attempt yields no successful receipt. Duplicate pay cannot create duplicate receipt. Equal, percent and custom splits have tests. Before live integration: authenticated participant authorization, server validation, idempotency, reconciliation and partner approval.

## Research and validation plan
Measure time from bill entry to ready state, allocation errors, completion rate and participant comprehension. Test equal dinner, unequal food/shared appetizer, tax/tip change, absent friend and declined funding. Success targets are hypotheses: group can explain every charge; no unapproved amount; complete sample checkout within 60 seconds. No user tests conducted yet.

# Group checkout decision memo
Checked October 15, 2026, Pacific. First-party claims, not independent product testing. No Split Bill provider approval or partnership exists.

## Verified facts
Cino QuickSplit advertises guest link/QR contributions with Apple/Google Pay and a virtual checkout card. Its current page lists €0.20 per transaction capped at €5 monthly, QuickSplit included. Older indexed copy showed sterling pricing: verify local terms before quoting UK fees. Its footer identifies Checkout SAS as debit-card issuer. No-app invitations and group-card checkout are competitive overlap.
https://www.getcino.com/quicksplit

Cino's support article (updated May 27, 2025) lists UK plus 29 European countries, not US. Homepage broadly agrees; QuickSplit's marketing counter says 33 countries. Exact count is inconsistent. US eligibility is not established. This suggests a positioning question, not verified demand or launch permission.
https://support.getcino.com/hc/en-us/articles/8255257055389-Which-countries-is-Cino-available-in
https://www.getcino.com/

Stripe checks Issuing balance/card controls before real-time authorization, whose decision window is two seconds. Approval reserves funds; capture creates a transaction; reversals/expiry release holds. Thus prepare contributions before merchant checkout, rather than collecting from participants during the authorization callback. Authorization is not final settlement, and this does not establish how consumer contributions fund a program.
https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/purchases/authorizations

Stripe wallet tokens require approved live cards, not sandbox cards. iOS push provisioning needs Apple's payment-pass entitlement. Android needs issuer onboarding, private SDK/API access and app allowlisting. Manual access precedes push access; backend short-lived keys and card/device eligibility checks are required. Issuer provisioning differs from merchant Apple Pay acceptance.
https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/cards/digital-wallets?platform=react-native

## Recommended architecture: hypothesis
Keep native simulation. Next: item assignments, exact tax/tip and versioned proposal; each person sees their total before approval. Material edits revoke approvals/card. Add validated local recovery/receipts, then authenticated membership and server-owned versions. Model funding readiness, authorization and capture separately in the future adapter. Live adapter stays disabled.

## Unresolved questions
- Eligible country/program, accountable cardholder and authorized spender? Separate from personal cards does not mean ownerless credit.
- Who carries failed/returned funding, liquidity, disputes, fees and refunds? Do not assume atomic multi-person collection.
- How are restaurant-tip changes and forced/late captures reconciled against consent caps?
- Does Cino offer item/shared-item allocation and immutable approval? Reviewed pages do not establish absence; no exclusivity claim.
- Does item-level consent motivate switching? Needs recruited user tests.

Research stop: enough evidence for next build. Repeat research only when a concrete decision needs it.

# Native app and group-card specification
Updated October 15, 2026. User direction: iOS/Android product with Venmo/Cash App familiarity, a dedicated group card and Apple/Google Pay.

## Intended experience
Create group checkout -> agree to shares -> secure contributions -> create/activate group card -> provision an authorized spender's wallet -> merchant payment -> reconciliation and individual receipts.
The card is separate from participants' existing personal cards. It cannot be literally ownerless: it must be associated with the issuer's approved cardholder/program. The issuer must agree to liability, funding and authorized spenders. A named authorized payer is the starting hypothesis. Do not assume all members can share a card or token. A credit card requires a real credit arrangement; prepaid/debit/credit structure remains unresolved. Demo language is “group card.”

## Delivered foundation
October 16 recovery update: local draft and simulated receipt snapshots now survive reopening. Approvals, card and wallet state deliberately do not; all participants must be simulated approving again. Local storage is not synchronized consent or a real wallet connection. Current design tokens are in DESIGN.md and supersede the early green palette described below.
Expo SDK 58 / React Native under mobile/, with Expo Router and shared native/web components. Home, Split, Card, Activity, Profile. Original Split Bill branding: green-led palette, bottom tabs, friend rows, large totals and card visual. The state reducer requires approvals, generates a demo session, gates checkout on simulated wallet setup, supports freezing/declines, blocks duplicate payments and revokes card/approvals when a split changes. No auth, real accounts, wallet tokens or native binary. State is in memory.

## Wallet research
Stripe supports eligible issued cards in digital wallets. Its documentation says wallet tokens require live mode and cannot be tested in a sandbox. iOS push provisioning requires Apple's payment-pass-provisioning entitlement. Android requires issuer/API access and native integration. Confirm program and region eligibility. Only show real wallet provisioning buttons when card/device eligibility is verified. This is issuer-side provisioning, not accepting Apple Pay as a merchant or generating a generic Wallet pass.
Sources checked October 15, 2026:

- https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/consumer-compliance
- https://docs.expo.dev/versions/v58.0.0/

# Split Bill design system and UX audit
Updated October 15, 2026. This specification is binding guidance for ongoing design work; preserve the native app as canonical.

## Research findings
“Vibecoded” is an informal judgment, not a measurable interface category. Microsoft Research's March 2026 paper examines homogenization risks and proposes deliberate challenges to default outputs; it does not establish that one color/font proves AI authorship. NN/g's visual-design guidance emphasizes typographic consistency, grid alignment, hierarchy and restrained palettes. Its consistency heuristic favors predictable conventions. Apply those principles to the task, rather than copying another app's screen.
Sources:
- https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/interrogating-design-homogenization-in-web-vibe-coding/
- https://www.nngroup.com/articles/why-does-design-look-good/
- https://www.nngroup.com/articles/visual-hierarchy-ux-definition/
- https://www.nngroup.com/articles/consistency-and-standards/

## Audit of previous implementation (source-based, not user testing)
1. Large slogan titles displaced useful information on every screen.
2. Nearly all content used similarly rounded colored boxes, flattening hierarchy.
3. Unicode glyphs used as navigation icons differed in weight, alignment and rendering.
4. Every action looked primary; three large approval buttons dominated the split screen.
5. Repeated implementation explanations and simulation warnings competed with task content.
6. Excessive bold weights, weak secondary-text contrast, arbitrary radii and spacing made screens feel assembled rather than designed.
7. Long screens buried the main action. Profile was unnecessarily a fifth navigation tab while already available through the avatar.

## Direction: a focused social payments utility
Quiet white canvas, charcoal ink, cobalt action color. Warm participant colors add human distinction without fake photos. Group-card art uses dark navy with simple concentric arcs as an intentional physical-card detail. Real tasks lead: active bill, your share, approvals, wallet choice, receipt. No invented transaction history, testimonials or balances.

## Tokens
Typography: DM Sans Regular / Medium / Bold, bundled locally for native and web. Money uses tabular numerals and a 58/68 display scale; screens use 28/35; section titles 17/24; body 15/22; supporting text 12/18. Do not add additional typefaces or font weights without a purpose.
Color: ink #171a20; action #2459e8; muted #626a78; divider #e8ebf0; surface #f5f6f8; positive #17794c. Accent color is reserved for actions/selection, not large decorative blocks on every screen.
Spacing: 4/8/12/16/24/32 scale, 24-point screen inset. Inputs and buttons at least 48/52 points; interactive approval targets 44 points high. Radius: 10 inputs, 12 buttons, 14 secondary panels, 18 active bill, 20 payment card. Standard Feather icons at 18–24 points.

## Interaction rules
- Four bottom destinations: Home, Split, Card, Activity. Profile via avatar.
- One main action in a persistent footer on checkout screens.
- Bill edit fields live behind an explicit Edit bill disclosure, not in the first-view foreground.
- Equal / percentage / amount selector exposes selected state.
- People use aligned rows; inline approval actions retain disabled/approved states.
- Wallet choices are selection rows; choose first, then simulate payment. Do not use official provisioning branding or imply real wallet connection.
- Decline scenario lives behind Demo scenarios; freeze is a standard card control.
- Persistent Demo badge plus contextual no-money text; technical implementation detail lives in profile and project docs.
- Empty activity has an honest empty state and a clear next action. Receipt only appears after simulated success.
- Keep all engine invariants: approval reset, invalid-input blocks, freeze and wallet gates, decline/retry, duplicate guard.
